text:
Priya N: Quick heads-up from load test — tiny requests (<=24 tokens) hitting horrible p99 during heavy coalescing. Proposal: microgrant fastpath (short-lived execution grant) to let tiny requests skip batch assembly for a tiny window. Thoughts?

Jonas L: Love the idea in principle. We need a tight accounting model so microgrants don't eat throughput. Token-equivalent credits + decay seems right. Also add a per-tenant active_microgrant cap.

Mia K: Can you share numbers? what's the observable delta?

Priya N: From last night: isolated small median ~6ms, under packer pressure median ~38ms, p99 ~320ms. Sample log:

```
q_len=380 in_flight=92 req_tokens=12 latency_ms=320 path=coalescer
q_len=380 in_flight=92 req_tokens=192 latency_ms=48 path=batch
```

Jonas L: Two immediate design constraints: 1) microgrant must be O(1) to grant/revoke (no heavy locking), 2) preemption path should be cheap (don't re-enqueue synchronously). Use an atomic slot ring per worker + CAS updates, signal executor via eventfd.

Mia K: On preemption semantics we should distinguish soft-revocation vs. force-kill. Soft-revocation asks executor to finish quickly and avoid new KV cache loads; force-kill is rare. Both need distinct telemetry tags.

Priya N: Proposed API sketch: `Request.obtain_microgrant(max_tokens, window_ms)` -> {ok:boolean, grant_id:opt}. `Microgrant.revoke(grant_id, mode)` where mode in {SOFT, FORCE} returns bool. We'll also expose `grant_state` enum for telemetry.

Jonas L: Backoff state: after a revoke, the request should enter a backoff window before trying again. Suggest exponential backoff with jitter: base 30ms * 2^k, cap 250ms. Keep tenant-level counters so noisy tenants don't hog retry attempts.

Mia K: Observability: emit counters/hists: `microgrant_granted_total`, `microgrant_revoked_total{mode}`, `microgrant_backoff_ms`, and `microgrant_gpu_util_delta` (gauge). Also sample events with `grant_id`, `tenant_id`, `route`, `revoked_by_batch` tag.

Priya N: Experiment snapshot from canary: microgrant v0.1 reduced tiny-req p99 from 320ms -> 52ms; aggregate throughput change -1.9% (within expected). ops-bot logged test: run-231.

ops-bot: canary-run:231 finished. small_req_p99: 320 -> 52 ms, total_throughput: -1.9%.

Jonas L: Nice. Rules to avoid thrash: 1) cap concurrent microgrants per worker and per-tenant; 2) prevent reclaim storms by staggering revoke signals; 3) prefer revoking microgrants with highest backoff penalty first.

Mia K: Implementation note: admission layer should make grant decision before coalescer enqueue. Keep grant state lightweight: (grant_id, expiry_ts, owner_worker, token_charge). Token charge deducted from tenant credit pool; credits replenish over time (token-bucket). If credits exhausted, deny grants.

Priya N: Edge cases: a) grant handed out but executor blocked on KV blocking op -> increases latency, b) many grants then a huge batch arrives and we revoke a bunch causing re-enqueue storm. Mitigations: short ttl (20-60ms), revoke soft by default, add revocation hysteresis (recently_revoked flag) to avoid immediate reclaim.

Jonas L: For durable correctness, implement idempotent revoke: CAS from GRANTED -> REVOKING -> REVOKED. Executors poll or get signalled to transition. If CAS fails, someone else handled it. Keep tracing spans with `microgrant.lifecycle` for root cause analysis.

Mia K: Rollout plan idea: config flag per-route `microgrant: {enabled, token_limit, window_ms, max_active}`. Canary on latency-critical routes first. Gate: small-req p99 reduced >=50% and throughput regression <2.5% for 12h.

Priya N: Action items: Priya to draft RFC with API + telemetry + failure modes. Jonas will prototype ring-slot CAS and signalging. Mia will add route config + gating in console. Target: stage canary in 6 days.

Jonas L: I'll add a microbench for CAS latencies and eventfd wake patterns. If revoke tail is >1ms often, we need different signalling.

Mia K: Add a snackable FAQ entry for customers: why some tiny requests still wait (credits/backoff) and how to tune route limits.

Priya N: Thanks! I'll post the RFC link when ready and include the perf dashboards + sample workload. @Mia K @Jonas L feel free to DM for pairing.
